reviews.pob: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. And the years of Kohath’s life were one hundred thirty-three years.
reviews.gloss: And sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel; and years of Kohath's life, three and thirty and a hundred years.
reviews.candidate: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived one hundred thirty-three years.
rubric: Names, parentage and lifespan 133 are preserved.
English copulas and reordered numerals express the source without a demonstrated addition or omission.
Does not resolve compressed-genealogy chronology or broader sons/descendants questions.
Current repetition preserves the local lifespan formula.
Shorter candidate is smoother; current text is intelligible.
Current formula matches 6:16 and 6:20; no corpus-wide claim.
reviews.countercase: Current repetition is cumbersome; shorter English improves ease. Equivalent meaning and loss of the repeated formula make this a stylistic tie.
reviews.confidence: High local fidelity; moderate tie classification; no earliest-source assessment.
reviews.reopen: Genealogy-specific linguistic or reader-comprehension evidence demonstrating a material misunderstanding.

reviews.source: וְ/עַל֙ גְּב֣וּל גָּ֔ד אֶל פְּאַ֖ת נֶ֣גֶב תֵּימָ֑נָ/ה וְ/הָיָ֨ה גְב֜וּל מִ/תָּמָ֗ר מֵ֚י מְרִיבַ֣ת קָדֵ֔שׁ נַחֲלָ֖ה עַל הַ/יָּ֥ם הַ/גָּדֽוֹל־־׃
reviews.pob: And along the border of Gad[a], on the south side southward, the border shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, to the Wadi of Egypt[b], and on to the Great Sea.
reviews.gloss: And along Gad's boundary, toward the southern side southward, the boundary shall be from Tamar, the waters of Meribath-kadesh, toward the wadi/watercourse, to the Great Sea.
reviews.candidate: And along the border of Gad, on the south side southward, the border shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh[a], to the wadi[b], and on to the Great Sea.
rubric: Landmark sequence and boundary course are preserved. Egypt is a defensible contextual identification.
No explicit Egypt word exists; absence alone does not make the inferred referent unsupported.
Current wording hides that identification is inferred; a qualified note can disclose this.
Both retain the repeated southern boundary description.
Removing Egypt reduces geographic intelligibility for readers skipping notes.
47:19 uses wadi; uniformity alone does not establish semantic gain.
reviews.countercase: Readers can mistake the inferred Egypt identification for an explicit Hebrew name, especially while disclosure is unapplied. Retention is permissible, not proven optimal; a source-qualified note addresses that objection.
reviews.confidence: High absence of explicit Egypt; moderate preferred disclosure; exact localization and syntax remain uncertain.
reviews.reopen: Passage-specific geographic/syntactic evidence undermining identification, or reader evidence demonstrating material misunderstanding.

ancillary.preferred_main: And along the border of Gad, on the south side southward, the border shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh[a], to the Wadi of Egypt[b], and on to the Great Sea.
ancillary.note_a: Move existing place-name alternative from Gad to Meribath-kadesh; retain existing note body.
ancillary.note_b: Or ‘brook.’ The Hebrew names a wadi or watercourse without ‘of Egypt’; identification with the Wadi of Egypt is contextual. A wadi is a streambed or watercourse, often seasonal.
ancillary.reasoning_history: Assessor initially considered deleting Egypt; the contextual-identification countercase favored retention with explicit disclosure. This is development of one assessment, not independent votes.

reviews.candidate_regression: Unnamed main-text watercourse loses geographic specificity unless notes read.
reviews.reference_role: Published interpretation/lexicon or annotation controls, not additional ancient witnesses.

reviews.source: וַ/יְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַ/יָּ֕מָת נָחָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵי עַמּ֑וֹן וַ/יִּמְלֹ֥ךְ בְּנ֖/וֹ תַּחְתָּֽי/ו־־׃
reviews.pob: After this, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son reigned in his place.
reviews.gloss: And it happened after this: Nahash king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son reigned/became king in his place.
reviews.candidate: After this, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place.
rubric: Both assign death to Nahash and replacement kingship to his son.
Neither adds Hanun, coronation, duration or a precise interval.
Accession is contextually supported, not required by Qal wayyiqtol morphology alone.
Both explain the subsequent condolence mission.
Became king is modestly clearer; reigned in his place remains intelligible.
Samuel parallel uses became king, but is another composition, not an independent Chronicles witness.
reviews.countercase: Reigned could emphasize a period rather than accession. In this complete death-and-replacement sentence, however, succession is already conveyed; modest clarity is not demonstrated semantic correction.
reviews.confidence: High fidelity and candidate permissibility; moderate tie classification.
reviews.reopen: Linguistic or reader evidence of obscured accession, or an explicit justified project consistency policy.
reviews.candidate_regression: No demonstrated semantic regression; stylistic/literary tradeoff remains.
reviews.reference_role: Published interpretation/lexicon or annotation controls, not additional ancient witnesses.
